content: Grommets, also known as ventilation tubes or tympanostomy tubes, are small cylindrical devices surgically inserted into the tympanic membrane (eardrum). These tubes are used as a treatment option for children who experience recurrent episodes of acute otitis media (middle ear infection). The primary purpose of grommets is to ventilate the middle ear and prevent the accumulation of fluid, which can contribute to repeated infections. By maintaining aeration of the middle ear, grommets help to reduce the frequency and severity of infections, alleviate associated symptoms, and improve hearing in affected children. The procedure to insert grommets is typically performed under general anesthesia and is considered safe and effective for managing recurrent acute otitis media.
